rv.q: The show is a homecoming; his gleefully deconstructed melodrama “An Octoroon,” produced at Soho Rep in 2014, made his reputation.

In addition to these fine performances and staging, what lends Gatz extra distinction that previous adaptations of the book cannot produce is the considerable beauty and incidental humor of Fitzgerald’s wordplay, spoken here in its entirety.
It is indeed one of the most tectonic-shifting, awe-inspiring stage works I’ll have ever seen.
The sense of simultaneous relief and satisfaction you'll feel at the end of this theatrical endurance test is very much worth experiencing live, whether for the first time or all over again.
A performance of such unforced sheen may not appear elsewhere in Manhattan right now.
Gatz is a long but worthwhile way to experience it in its fullness, made even richer with Collins's staging.
If you also have an appetite for ambitious or unusual theater projects and, in particular, marathon theater events, it would be foolhardy to not to see it and savor every moment.
Gatz is like nothing I’ve ever experienced before; I now understand why so many friends and colleagues have seen it multiple times.

cn.t: Critics hail this word-for-word, eight-hour adaptation of The Great Gatsby as a remarkable theatrical achievement. While not for every taste, the production generates atmospheric magic that offers a profound counterpoint to Broadway's glitzier Gatsby musical.

vr.q: One of those legendary theater experiences that I honestly think everyone should see at some point.
But if you're up for it, it is definitely worth your while, especially since it's likely gonna be the last time this production is staged in New York.
